philosophy: Learn reusable writing techniques, not article content or publisher expression.
boundaries: Do not memorize article bodies, publisher phrasing, or publisher headline structure.
Store craft principles, issue frequencies, success rates, and prevention rules only.
Use the Story Dossier for facts and the Writing Pattern Library for technique.

lead.principle: Start with the most newsworthy verified fact and reach the point within two sentences.
lead.teachWriter: Start with the most newsworthy verified fact and reach the point within two sentences.

structure.principle: Answer who, what, when, and where before context or analysis.
structure.teachWriter: Answer who, what, when, and where before context or analysis.

transition.principle: Move from facts to context before analysis, without repeating the same sentence function.
transition.teachWriter: Move from facts to context before analysis, without repeating the same sentence function.

evidence.principle: Attribute claims, separate confirmed facts from developing information, and qualify single-source details.
evidence.teachWriter: Attribute claims, separate confirmed facts from developing information, and qualify single-source details.

headline.principle: Create headlines from the completed CE story dossier using actor + action + consequence.
headline.teachWriter: Build the headline after the article/dossier is complete; do not rewrite from publisher headlines.

ending.principle: End with why the confirmed development matters or what verified next step readers should watch.
ending.teachWriter: End with why the confirmed development matters or what verified next step readers should watch.
